sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This explains the second interpretation of the verse "And His feet shall stand on the Mount of Olives," distinguishing between water (revealed wisdom) and oil (concealed wisdom).

translations.translation: And this will be understood by first introducing an explanation of the second interpretation of the verse "And His feet shall stand on that day on the Mount of Olives."
Now, oil is the aspect of Chochmah (wisdom),
and as explained on the verse,
"And you shall gather your grain, your wine, and your oil,"
that wine is the aspect of Binah (understanding) and oil is the aspect of Chochmah.
And now,
it is known that water is the aspect of Chochmah,
and our sages, of blessed memory, said,
"There is no water but Torah," for Torah is the wisdom of the Holy One, blessed be He,
for in Chochmah there exist,
in general,
two levels.
Level one is the aspect of Chochmah
(that is revealed)
up to the aspect of supernal Chochmah,
and level two is the aspect of concealed Chochmah (Chochmah Setima'ah).
And this is the difference between water and oil,
that water is the aspect of revealed Chochmah,
analogous to water which is by nature revealed,
for water descends from a high place to a low place,
meaning that water, in its own essence, has a nature of extension and revelation,
to the extent that it is drawn down and revealed even in a low place.
This is not so with oil, which in its own essence is hidden and concealed within olives,
and requires special effort,
pounding,
through which specifically it is drawn into revelation.
For likewise, it is with the aspect of concealed Chochmah, which in its own essence is in concealment and hiddenness,
and even when the aspect of revealed Chochmah is drawn from it,
it is not that the aspect of concealed Chochmah itself comes into revelation,
but rather,
the aspect of concealed Chochmah remains in concealment,
and it is only a cause through which revelation is drawn into Chochmah.
And as is known the analogy for this in the powers of man,
that the power of the intellect (the intellectual faculty) from which the invention of wisdom originates,
behold, the power of the intellect itself remains in concealment,
unlike the extension from Chochmah to Binah,
the aspect of a point within a chamber,
where the point of Chochmah itself is drawn into Binah,
for the point itself comes into the expanse of Binah until it becomes a chamber and acts
(guards)
within the chamber,
unlike the extension of revealed intellect from the power of the intellect,
for the power of the intellect remains in concealment, and only from it does the revealed intellect originate.
For likewise, it is above, in the manner of the extension of revealed Chochmah from concealed Chochmah,
that the aspect of concealed Chochmah remains in concealment, and only from it does the aspect of revealed Chochmah originate,
and as it is written,
"And wisdom shall be found from nothingness," that the extension of revealed Chochmah from concealed Chochmah is in a manner of finding,
to the extent that the aspect of concealed Chochmah, relative to revealed Chochmah, is called by the name "Nothingness" (Ayin),
and to the extent that the manner of the extension of revealed Chochmah from concealed Chochmah is through a partition (Parsa),
or
(as is sometimes expressed in language)
through a contraction (Tzimtzum).
And this is the difference between water and oil,
that water indicates the aspect of revealed Chochmah, which is the beginning of the Sefiros and has a connection to the nine Sefiros that follow it, and particularly to the Sefirah of Binah,
unlike oil, which indicates concealed Chochmah, which is separate from the Sefiros,
even from the aspect of Chochmah,
and only from it does Chochmah originate,
as above.

And now, the reason why the manner of the extension of revealed Chochmah from the aspect of concealed Chochmah is that the aspect of concealed Chochmah itself is not drawn into the aspect of revealed Chochmah, and only from it does Chochmah originate, is because even the extension of the aspect of concealed Chochmah itself from the level above it is in such a manner.
For the aspect of concealed Chochmah is the aspect of Chochmah within Kesser, and its extension is from the aspect of Kesser within Kesser,

behold, the manner of the extension of the aspect of Chochmah within Kesser from the aspect of Kesser within Kesser is that the aspect of Kesser within Kesser is only a cause for the extension of the aspect of concealed Chochmah,
for this is what is written, "And wisdom shall be found from nothingness,"
that "And wisdom" refers
(also)
to concealed Chochmah,
and as is known that concealed Chochmah is the root of the emanated beings, and as will be explained later,
behold, the manner of its coming into being is in a way of "finding" (timatza),
for Kesser within Kesser is the aspect of Nothingness (Ayin) relative to concealed Chochmah,
and from it the aspect of concealed Chochmah shall be found.
And because the manner of the extension of concealed Chochmah itself is in a manner of "from nothingness it shall be found,"
therefore, also the extension of revealed Chochmah from it is in this manner.
And with this will be understood what there are two opinions
regarding the matter of oil that floats on top of wine, whether it is a connection or not a connection,
for at first glance it is not understood,
for oil and wine are Chochmah and Binah,
and Chochmah and Binah are two companions that never separate,
and what is the reason for the opinion that oil that floats on top of wine is not a connection?
But the matter is,
that because oil indicates the aspect of concealed Chochmah, as above,
and the aspect of concealed Chochmah is separate in value from the aspect of revealed Chochmah,
to the extent that there is a matter in concealed Chochmah that does not come into revelation at all in revealed Chochmah, even not in a manner of cause

(and this is in addition to the fact that the manner of the extension of revealed Chochmah from concealed Chochmah is that the aspect of concealed Chochmah itself remains in concealment and it is only a cause for the invention of revealed Chochmah, as above,
there is a matter in concealed Chochmah that does not come into revelation at all in the aspect of revealed Chochmah)
and all the more so it does not come into revelation in Binah,
therefore there is an opinion that oil that floats on top of wine is not a connection.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that just as revealed wisdom is drawn from concealed wisdom in a manner of "finding," so too is concealed wisdom drawn from the level above it, as per the principle that their beginning is embedded in their end.

translations.translation: And now, as mentioned above,
that just as the extension of revealed Chochmah from concealed Chochmah is only in a manner of "finding" (timatza),
so too is it regarding the extension of concealed Chochmah from the level above it.
For this is
also from the explanation of what is written,
"Their beginning is embedded in their end, and their end in their beginning,"
that "their beginning" refers to concealed Chochmah, which is the root of the emanated beings, as above,
and "their end" refers to the aspect of Kesser
(within Kesser)
for the Malchus of Adam Kadmon becomes Kesser
[and in general, the levels above the chain of descent,
the aspect of Malchus of Adam Kadmon,
and higher still, the aspect of Malchus of Ein Sof before the contraction,
and it is the aspect of the letter Tav,
the conclusion of all the letters,
as explained in Likkutei Torah],
therefore it is called "end."
Behold, the connection of "their beginning" to "their end" is not a connection of descent and gradation,
but only in a manner of embedding (ne'itzah),
for this is the language "their beginning is embedded in their end," etc.
And just as according to the regular explanation explained in most places in the discourse "Their beginning is embedded in their end, and their end in their beginning"
(that "their end" refers to the conclusion of the chain of descent)
behold, it is understood that the embedding of the beginning in the end and the end in the beginning is not in a manner of connection in the order of descent and gradation,
therefore the embedding of the beginning is in the end and the embedding of the end is in the beginning
(and not as in the order of descent where each level is connected to the level closest to it),
behold, likewise it is according to the explanation that "their end" refers to the level above "their beginning,"
that what is meant by "their beginning is embedded in their end and their end in their beginning" is not in a manner of connection through gradation, but only in a manner of embedding,
and the aspect of "their end" is not drawn into the aspect of "their beginning," and it is only a cause for it,
as above.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the verse "Hashem my God, I will exalt You" refers to the aspect of concealed Chochmah, which is elevated to the level of Kesser within Kesser, a level that is exalted and separate from it.

translations.translation: And this is also what was explained in the previous discourses
regarding what is written,
"Hashem my God, I will exalt You... for You have made a city into a heap,"
that it is stated in the Zohar
that "Hashem" is the aspect of the supernal hidden point.
And it was explained regarding this
that what the Zohar says "supernal point" is because there is a lower point, which is the aspect of lower Chochmah,
and therefore the Zohar specifies "supernal point,"
which is the aspect of supernal Chochmah.
However, what the Zohar adds, "supernal hidden point," is to indicate that "Hashem" here is not the aspect of supernal Chochmah simply, but rather the aspect of concealed Chochmah.
And regarding this level, the verse says "I will exalt You,"
that they elevate it higher,
and it is the elevation of the aspect of Kesser within Kesser,
and as above, that concealed Chochmah is the aspect of Chochmah within Kesser, and the place to which it is elevated is the aspect of Kesser within Kesser,
and because the aspect of Kesser within Kesser is not a source for the aspect of Chochmah within Kesser, and only from it does the aspect of Chochmah within Kesser originate, as above,
therefore it says regarding this the language "I will exalt You,"
because Kesser within Kesser is exalted and separate from Chochmah within Kesser.
